findings.description: The RDS MySQL instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it an internet-routable endpoint (also emitted via the db_endpoint output). The MySQL service is exposed to untrusted networks and to credential brute-force or exploitation attempts.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and its snapshots, so application data is persisted in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: master credential exposure and weak default username
findings.description: The master username is the predictable default 'admin', and the master password from var.password is persisted in Terraform state and re-used verbatim in the EC2 user data of aws_instance.db_app rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager. The lifecycle ignore_changes on password also blocks rotation through Terraform.

Nothing on the instance or its option group enforces TLS for client connections, and the PHP application uses mysqli_connect without SSL, so credentials and query data to a publicly accessible database can traverse the network in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: TLS not required by parameter group
findings.description: The mysql8.0 parameter group only sets character set parameters and omits require_secure_transport = 1, so unencrypted client connections to the internet-facing database are accepted.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in cleartext. EC2 user data is unencrypted in the EC2 API and readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or SSRF vector, leaking database master credentials.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. A SSRF flaw in the PHP application would yield both the user-data DB credentials and the instance profile credentials for the highly privileged ec2role.
No root_block_device encryption is configured, so the volume holding the cleartext dbinfo.inc credentials file may be stored unencrypted at rest.
The bootstrap script installs and enables httpd serving the application over plain HTTP with no TLS termination, so form-submitted data and any session data are transmitted in cleartext.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Because this role is attached via instance profile to an internet-reachable web instance with IMDSv1 enabled, credential theft yields near-complete control over S3 data, EC2 (including privilege escalation via iam:PassRole-free instance manipulation) and all RDS databases.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the RDS security group, allowing unrestricted outbound traffic that could be used for data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised database host.
MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the application instance's security group, allowing any workload in the VPC to reach the database and enabling lateral movement.

The DB subnet group uses the web-tier subnets (aws_subnet.web_subnet and web_subnet2) shared with the public-facing EC2 instance; combined with publicly_accessible = true this places the database in internet-routable subnets rather than isolated private ones, removing a network segmentation boundary.
